title: LIVE UPDATES: Undas 2026 (Nov. 2, 2026)
summary: Filipinos observe All Souls' Day on November 2, Monday, by going to cemeteries to remember their departed relatives. Here are the latest news and updates.

People continue to visit the Pasig Catholic Cemetery for Undas 2026. Carlo Mateo/Super Radyo dzBB
Over 65,000 visitors visited Pasig Catholic Cemetery on Nov. 1
#Undas2026: Bilang ng mga dumalaw sa Pasig Catholic Cemetery kahapon, umabot sa mahigit 65,000. | via @SurfaceCarlo https://t.co/IAJgfJDUxR — DZBB Super Radyo (@dzbb) November 1, 2026
Number coding suspended on Nov. 2, All Souls' Day —MMDA
The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) on Thursday announced that the implementation of the number coding scheme will be suspended on Monday, November 2.
November 2, All Souls Day, was declared as a special non-working holiday.
"Awtomatikong sinususpinde ang number coding tuwing regular at special non-working holidays," MMDA said.
(The number coding scheme is automatically suspended during regular and special non-working holidays.)
The Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX) is expecting around 1.9 million passengers this year amid the exodus for this year's Undas break.

Meanwhile, several passengers have started traveling to the provinces more than a week ahead of Undas, filling bus terminals early either to beat the holiday rush or to secure their tickets before the surge of crowds. —VAL, GMA News

Isolated rains over extreme Northern Luzon due to Northeast Monsoon
The Northeast Monsoon or Amihan will bring cloudy skies with isolated rains over parts of extreme Northern Luzon on Monday, PAGASA reported.
Meanwhile, the state weather bureau continues to monitor the tropical cyclone outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR).

Typhoon IN-FA (2631) is located at 2,175 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon, packing maxium sustained winds of 140 kilometers per hour, gustiness of up to 170 km/h, and moving westward at the speed of 15 km/h.
Forecast weather conditions
Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, and Cagayan Valley will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated light rains due to the northeast monsoon but with no significant impact.

Metro Manila and the rest of the country will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms due to localized thunderstorms and flash floods or landslides may occur during severe thunderstorms.
Forecast wind and coastal water conditions
The whole country will experience light to moderate wind speed moving in the northeast to east direction while coastal waters will remain slight to moderate.
Sunrise will be at 5:52 a.m., sunset at 5:27 p.m. — BAP, GMA News
